title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: monitor agents (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap scope, default policy behaviour, investigation permissions and auditing controls are supported. Minor corrections should complete the policy navigation, flag the Usage center preview and reconcile checklist controls with the table.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The policy is on by default for organisations with supported licences once the service is set up.
claims.quote: The Risky Agents (preview) policy is available by default to all organizations with supported licenses. When the service is set up, this policy is automatically present and ready to generate alerts based on observed agent activity.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Why it matters
claims.claim: The agent monitoring page names no cloud and gives no cloud-specific rollout details.
claims.quote: Searched: the full Monitoring agents in Insider Risk Management page for cloud, GCC, GCC High, DoD and rollout; it specifies supported agents and default policy availability, not clouds or cloud-specific rollout.

claims.claim: Learn's agent pages do not describe how the agent-specific insider risk score is calculated.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management agent risk score calculation; read monitoring-agents, policy-templates and agent-registry-overview. These describe detections, sharing and aggregated risk signals, not the agent-specific score calculation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Administrative units are not supported for agent alerts, so scoped analysts cannot see them.
claims.quote: Admins units are currently not supported for agent alerts. If a scoped analyst is signing in, then they can't see agent related alerts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Unscoped users with alert-investigation permissions can review agent alerts and detected activity.
claims.quote: Access & investigate alerts | Yes | No | Yes | Yes | No | No; Members who aren't assigned administrative units are unrestricted administrators and have access to all settings, policies, and user data.

claims.claim: Guest interactions expose only sensitive-information indicators, not full prompt and response content, for investigation.
claims.quote: When guest users are interacting with agents, the full prompt and response content isn't available for investigation. Instead, only indicators of sensitive information detected in those prompts and responses are shown.

claims.claim: Opening IRM alerts through agent-registry risk details requires IRM Analyst or IRM Investigator; Global Administrator alone is insufficient.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview — IRM alerts | IRM Analyst or IRM Investigator. Global Administrator alone is insufficient; a Global Administrator can assign themselves the additional IRM role.

claims.claim: The agent monitoring page describes investigation rather than agent blocking or remediation.
claims.quote: Searched: Risky Agents policy disable and Insider Risk Management policies API; read monitoring-agents and policies. Monitoring-agents describes investigation and deciding further action, not a blocking operation; Entra results concern a different risk service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft offers creation of a custom Insider Risk Management policy when the default does not fit organisational requirements.
claims.quote: If the default policy doesn't meet your organizational requirements, you can create a custom Insider Risk Management policy to better align with your risk posture or investigation needs.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Insider Risk Management uses pay-as-you-go billing, per-user licensing or both, supporting the mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: This feature uses pay-as-you-go billing or per-user licensing for Microsoft Purview capabilities or both.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Administrators must verify a supported subscription and assign appropriate user licences, following the linked subscription requirements.
claims.quote: To access and use Insider Risk Management, administrators need to verify their organization has a supported subscription and assign the appropriate licenses to users. For more information about subscriptions and licensing, see the subscription requirements

claims.claim: The setup page suggests a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 trial for organisations wanting to try Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: If you don't have an existing Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 plan and want to try Insider Risk Management, you can add Microsoft 365 to your existing subscription or sign up for a trial of Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5.

claims.claim: Agent monitoring requires completion of the Insider Risk Management setup steps, and its page links the setup licensing section.
claims.quote: Before you begin monitoring agents in your organization, you must complete the steps provided in Get started with Insider Risk Management. For information about subscriptions, licensing, and permissions, see Subscriptions and licensing

claims.claim: Some Insider Risk Management indicators require enabling pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Some indicators included in Insider Risk Management are only available if you enable the pay-as-you-go billing model for your organization.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal Usage center shows pay-as-you-go and per-user licensing usage.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview Usage center feature is in preview. ... You can view your pay-as-you-go billing usage and your per-user licensing usage for Microsoft Purview capabilities.
claims.fix: Call it 'the preview Usage center' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-billing-usage. The setup page establishes that the center exists but the usage page documents what it shows and its preview status.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate rate, meter or licence specific to the Risky Agents monitoring policy is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Risky Agents billing; Purview Risky Agents price license; Insider Risk Management agents licensing meter. Read monitoring-agents, billing-models, policy-indicators, service description and Azure Purview pricing; none specifies separate Risky Agents policy pricing.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record contains no licence information.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management is being expanded to agents, with specific indicators and insider risk score built for agents based on agentic activities.

claims.where: Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; controls[1].governs
claims.claim: Auditing is a prerequisite because Insider Risk Management policies and analytics use Microsoft 365 audit logs.
claims.quote: Step 2 (required): Enable the Microsoft 365 audit log ... Insider Risk Management uses Microsoft 365 audit logs for user insights and risk management activities identified in policies and analytics insights.

claims.claim: Auditing is on by default in Microsoft 365, except the named Business plans and unmanaged enterprise-trial tenants.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium. Additionally, unmanaged tenants that use free trials of enterprise licenses don't have auditing enabled by default.

claims.claim: Accessing and configuring recommended actions requires the Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Admins role group.
claims.quote: To access and configure recommended actions, users must be assigned to the Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Admins role groups.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Policies > Agent policy reaches the agent-policy dashboard.
claims.quote: go to Insider Risk Management > Policies ... Your policies are separated into two categories: User policy and Agent policy. Switch between the two to locate relevant policy details.
claims.fix: Keep the path and add to controls[0].note: 'This route ends at the agent-policy dashboard; select a policy to see its details.' The cited page says 'You can select the policy to see the health status details'; the printed route does not reach a policy-setting control.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for managing Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management policies API PowerShell Microsoft Graph; Risky Agents policy disable scope. Read monitoring-agents, policies and policy-indicators. No default-agent-policy disabling/scoping procedure or policy-management API found; Entra riskyAgents is different.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity enables auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables unified auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. ... Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to decide alert-investigation role groups, but the controls table has no permissions row.
claims.quote: Decide which role groups will investigate agent alerts ... [The table contains only Agent policies and unified audit logging.]
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Decide which role groups will investigate agent alerts, and keep scoped analysts away from this work because admin units do not support agent alerts.' Keep the existing role-planning advice in Why it matters; do not add a control row.

claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to check the Usage center, but the controls table has no usage-monitoring row.
claims.quote: Check the Usage center in the Microsoft Purview portal for any pay-as-you-go usage after agent alerts begin. [No Usage center row appears in the controls table.]
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet about checking the Usage center; retain the existing usage-checking advice in Cost and licensing. Do not add a control row.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management and Insider Risk Management Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote: Actions | Insider Risk Management | Insider Risk Management Admins | Insider Risk Management Analysts | Insider Risk Management Investigators ... Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes | No | No | No | No

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management role-group membership is managed on the role-groups page in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal ... Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane.

claims.claim: The policy dashboard separates user and agent policies into User policy and Agent policy views.
claims.quote: Your policies are separated into two categories: User policy and Agent policy. Switch between the two to locate relevant policy details. Agent policy covers agents from Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry.

claims.claim: Turning unified auditing off leaves no audit-log results for Insider Risk Management to read.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no setting or API to turn off or scope the default Risky Agents policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Risky Agents policy disable scope; Insider Risk Management policies API PowerShell Microsoft Graph. Read monitoring-agents, policies and policy-indicators. Custom policies and user-policy scoping are described, but no default Risky Agents disabling/scoping procedure is given.

claims.claim: The sources describe no change to the experience of ordinary users or agent users.
claims.quote: Searched: Risky Agents scope policy Purview; read monitoring-agents and policy-templates. They describe monitoring, detection and analyst investigation, not a changed user interface or a new user-facing action.

claims.claim: The roadmap has no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null
